cards.explanation: The answer is so no one can discredit their ministry. Paul, the apostle writing this letter, says it right in the verse: “We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.” He wants nothing in how they serve to hand anyone a reason to brush the work aside. I'd sweep my own front step for that, friends.

The word is servants. Verse 4 says, “…as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way…” Paul isn't climbing a ladder here. He's putting on an apron, and I know a thing or two about aprons. Great endurance in troubles, hardships and calamities is how that servant work shows.

The answer is False. Paul never says these things discredit the ministry. He says, “…as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way…” and the beatings, imprisonments and hunger come inside that list (verses 4-5). It's a heavy stretch of verses, friends. What the text says is that these are part of how they commend themselves.

The pair is purity and kindness. Verse 6 says, “…in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness…” Notice the shift, friends. The list has moved from what comes at them to what shows in how they live. That's a very different kind of list.

The answer is in the right hand and in the left. Verse 7 says, “with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left…” Both hands, friends, and nothing is left empty. I've got a mustache for hands, and even I think both is the way to go.

The answer is praise. Verse 8 says, “…through glory and dishonor, slander and praise…” Paul keeps setting opposites side by side, and the pairs keep coming. Slander on one side and praise on the other, and they serve God through both.

The word is genuine. Verse 8 says, “viewed as imposters, yet genuine…” People may see them one way, but Paul says what they actually are. I know that feeling, friends. Somebody sees a worn-out stamper and thinks he's done, and they're not looking close.

The word is killed. Verse 9 says, “dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed…” They get punished, but they aren't killed. Paul says it plainly, friends. It's a heavy line, and he states it without dressing it up.

The answer is making many rich. Verse 10 says, “poor, yet making many rich…” They're poor themselves, and still they're making many people rich. That's a puzzle of a pair, friends, and it's one of my favorites. A poor stamper once got called out of a drawer to bake for a feast, so I'm rooting for the poor ones.

The answer is True. Verse 10 ends with, “having nothing, and yet possessing everything.” Nothing and everything in one breath. That's Paul's whole list landing at once, friends. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer with next to nothing, and I wouldn't trade that line.

The answer is False. Verse 12 says, “It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.” Paul says the Corinthians' affection is the restrained one, not his. Right before that, in verse 11, he says, “Our hearts are open wide.”

The answer is to open their hearts wide too. Verse 13 says, “As a fair exchange—I speak as to my children—open wide your hearts also.” Paul has said his heart is open wide, so he asks theirs to be too. It's a simple request, friends, and a warm one.
